newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones adds 7 Chinese firms to HK index.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones adds 7 Chinese firms to HK index.

text.p: Seven Chinese stocks and four Hong Kong-based company stocks will replace 11 issues in the Dow Jones Hong Kong Stock Index effective July 1, when Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule, Dow Jones & Co said Thursday.
"Red chip" Chinese stocks are those of publicly held companies in China with Hong Kong operations and stocks listed for trading in Hong Kong.

The red chips being added to the Dow Jones Hong Kong Stock Index are: China Overseas Land and Investment Ltd; China Resources Enterprise Ltd; China Travel International Investment H.K. Ltd ; Cosco Pacific Ltd; Guangnan (Holdings) Ltd ; Guangzhou Investment Co Ltd; and Ng Fung Hong Ltd.
Hong Kong-headquartered companies joining the index are: Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd; Glorious Sun Enterprises Ltd; Ka Wah Bank Ltd and New World Infrastructure Ltd.

China Motor Bus Co Ltd ; Cross-Harbour Tunnel ; Jardine International Motor ; Lai Sun Garment ; Miramar Hotel & Investment Co ; New Asia Realty & Trust Co ; Stelux Holdings ; Tai Cheung Holdings Ltd ; Vtech Holdings; Wing Lung Bank Ltd ; and Wing On Co International.
The Dow Jones Hong Kong Stock Index is comprised of 67 stocks representing about 80 percent of the equity capital on the Hong Kong stock market, the world's 8th largest stock market.
The last component change to the Dow Jones Hong Kong Stock Index occurred November 3, 1996.

"This adjustment in the Dow Jones Hong Kong Stock Index reflects the significant political changes in Hong Kong and the broader Chinese investments that the Hong Kong market now encompasses," John Prestbo, editor of Dow Jones Global Indexes, said in a statement released Thursday.
